reason: MotionBricks subproject ships synthetic-data training scripts that read configs from the repo and can run a few steps on CPU with no gated resources.
demo: motionbricks/README.md Training: python scripts/train_vqvae.py and python scripts/train_root.py (synthetic data)
goal: Install the motionbricks subproject (cd motionbricks; pip install -e .) in a CPU-only environment, then make both `python scripts/train_vqvae.py --max_steps 20 --batch_size 4 --num_samples 40` and `python scripts/train_root.py --max_steps 20 --batch_size 4 --num_samples 40` run from the motionbricks directory to completion and print 'Training complete.'. Both scripts train on synthetic data using the configs under motionbricks/out/; train_pose.py (which needs the pretrained VQVAE checkpoint) is not required. Provide /work/env.sh that activates the environment.
check: Running the VQVAE and the root-model synthetic-data training for 20 steps each on CPU exits successfully, logs each start banner, reaches 20 steps and prints 'Training complete.' with no traceback.

revision.by: fairness review (every maintained-set exam re-checked against the source)
issues: Coverage is one of the two CPU-feasible training scripts. motionbricks/README.md Training lists train_vqvae.py, train_pose.py and train_root.py; train_root.py needs no checkpoint ('no VQVAE needed') and is just as cheap, but the oracle runs only train_vqvae.py, so a broken root-model/backbone path would still pass.
No correctness bug in the original oracle: the banner, 'Training complete.' and step-count greps match scripts/train_vqvae.py:131-135 and Lightning's max_steps stop message.

Note (not counted against the test): motionbricks/README.md:77 lists 'a CUDA-capable GPU' as a requirement, but the training scripts set accelerator='auto' and the run passed on CPU, so testing training is fine.
